text: Abdomen: air sacs (a thin, normally near-invisible transparent membrane) become cloudy and covered in mucus or pus in Colibacillosis, Mycoplasma, or Infectious Bronchitis. Liver: a slight green discoloration near the gall bladder is normal; disease signs include swollen and green (Salmonella), swollen with grey areas (Fowl Cholera), greyish nodules (Marek's disease), or a fibrin coating (Mycoplasma, Colibacillosis). Spleen: enlargement suggests Salmonellosis. Digestive tract: general intestinal inflammation suggests Salmonellosis; hemorrhages in the gizzard suggest Newcastle Disease; Ascaris worms are common in scavenging birds; ceca full of blood suggest Coccidiosis. Lungs: normally pink, becoming greyish in Salmonellosis or bloody in Fowl Cholera and Avian Influenza. Bursa of Fabricius (near the cloaca): swollen, hemorrhagic, with cheesy content in Gumboro disease.
